title: Administrative coordinator (F/M) - Ukraine
body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?  
For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

**MdM in Ukraine**

MdM International Network has been operating in Ukraine since 2014, improving access to health care, especially providing comprehensive Primary Health Care (PHC), Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) and Mental Health and Psychosocial support (MHPSS) services.

Since February 2022, MdM Spain is leading the country response for the network, while MdM-France is in charge of the operations in Southern Ukraine. The global strategy aims at ensuring the access to quality comprehensive healthcare services for the conflict-affected population in Ukraine.

In Southern Ukraine, MdM-France has set up its country office and a base office in Mykolaiv. An office in Odesa is still running for specific activities monitoring in Odesa. The program consists in supporting various local-based organizations in the delivery of health services for people facing severe constraints to healthcare in Mykolaev and Kherson Oblasts.

The main strategic objectives for the Adminisrative department are, to consolidate the operational process at mission level to strengthen the quality of support services, to transfer competencies to national staff as well as working closer with national partners to build capacities.

Living conditions in Mykolaiv are pleasant (access to restaurants, presence of other organizations, places to relax...).

Expats share modern, well-equiped guesthouse. However, there are strict security rules (curfew imposed by the authorities) and a volatile environment (regular activation of air alerts).

**About the role**

As Administrative Coordinator, you ensure completeness, correctness, timeliness and integrity in your role. As a strategic partner to the operations, you will contribute to the definition and implementation of the mission’s objectives, participate in the sizing of the HR and financial needs and provide technical support to operational staff on the HR and Financial management of the mission.

**What you’ll do**

More specifically, your main responsibilities are the following:

- Nationalize the administrative coordinator position
- Review & implement a new HR set up of Finance & HR department post nationalization
- Supervise the implementation of the mission’s HR set-up
- Define, adapt, plan, and supervise the implementation of the mission’s human resources frameworks, procedures and policies while respecting the local context, local legislation and MdM policies and values (compensations and benefits, recruitment good practices, performance reviews, staff safe guarding, talent management, staff disciplines, career development and learning or team building)
- Plan, centralize, coordinate, and supervise the financial management and administration of the mission (accounting, budget construction and follow-up, internal and external reporting, donor compliance, audits, administrative legal obligations, etc.)
- Follow up the evolution of the legal environment and ensure MdM remains in line with official guidelines and policies in the framework of its principled approach
- Recruit, train, and manage an administrative department team
- Provide technical support to operational staff on the HR and financial management of the mission
- In terms of coordination and representation, you will ensure, when needed and by delegation of the General Coordinator, the representation of MdM in front of donors and liaise with INGOs heads of Admin Departments in-country
- You will provide strong oversight to MDM local Partner activities, including compliance with donor regulations

**Who you’ll work with**

Under the supervision of the General Coordinator (F/M), you will manage the HR and Finance team in the coordination office and functionally support the HR and Finance team in the operational base(s). You will closely interact with the HR and Finance Advisors based in the HQ and the other departments at mission level (logistics, programs etc.)

## REQUIREMENTS

**You are the right match if you:**

- hold a 3 years’ higher education management qualification
- have at least 4 years of experience in administration (HR and Finance) in a humanitarian context (including at least two years’ experience in an international NGO at coordination level)
- have an experience in a conflict setting or challenging environment. like in Ukraine (strong asset)
- have previous experience with MdM (preferred)
- proved your ability to negotiate and build / consolidate a network with authorities in a complex and volatile legal environment
- have a previous successful experience in team management (preferred)
- have a significant experience in PSEA management (an advantage)
- have a solid experience in budget management backed by institutional donors, payroll and accounting in a humanitarian context (prerequisite)
- you proved you are able to understand and interpret the legal administrative framework for staff and the MdM rules
- you have excellent Microsoft Office skills (especially Excel) and knowledge of accountancy software (like Saga or any relevant ERP)
- are fluent in English (mandatory, C1 level minimum), and have some knowledge of Ukrainian and/or Russian (would be an asset

**This role may not suit you if:**

- you are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach
- you are not able to defend the Administrative point of you in front of other actors/leaders
- you are not diplomatic and assertive

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow during the month of November.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.  
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

## EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: 3'392 €
- Fixed-term contract (6 months), starting in beginning of December
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Mykolaiv
- Regular field visits

**Benefits**:

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: guesthouse managed by the mission
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

**Essentials**:

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.  
if you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

title: Medical coordinator (F/M) - Sudan
body:
For more than 40 years, Médecins du Monde (MdM), a campaigning medical organisation committed to international solidarity, has been caring for the most vulnerable populations here and abroad. It has continued to bear witness to obstacles that exist in accessing healthcare and has secured sustainable improvements in health-for-all policies.

Those working for this independent organisation do not solely dispense care and treatment but condemn violations of human dignity and rights and fight to improve matters for populations living in precarious situations.

MdM France currently works in 30 countries across all continents to facilitate access to healthcare through 6 political battles:

- Sexual and Reproductive Health Rights
- Migration, Exile, Human Rights and Health
- Harm Reduction
- Environment and Health
- Humanitarian Space
- Healthcare systems and rights

**MdM in Sudan**

MdM maintained a presence in Jebel Marra until 2011. Mid-December 2025, MdM decided to launch an exploratory mission in West Darfur and allocated core funds to provide medicines, recruit an exploratory team composed of a head of mission, a medical coordinator and a logistics coordinator, and start activities in Darfur.

Since end of April 2026, MdM is managing a clinic in the Dar Omo camp in Feina (South Darfur) hosting approximately 25.000 displaced persons.

Since August 2026, 2 mobile clinics are operating around Feina and mid-September 2026, MdM has launched a response to a cholera outbreak in North Darfur.

MdM France has decided to register itself and consolidate its presence in East Sudan to have a balanced presence in all Sudan and be able to answer humanitarian needs in this part of the country.

**About the role**

You are in charge of designing, planning, implementing, adapting and monitoring health activities. You directly manage the medical team.

**What you’ll do**

- Participate in the definition of the country strategy led by the general coordinator and drive the medical and technical aspects in the development of this strategy
- Design, plan, implement, adapt and monitor the programme’s health activities
- Ensure the quality and relevance of health activities, supervise the collection and analysis of medical data
- Recruit, manage, train, and motivate the medical team
- Ensure the management of pharmaceutical products
- Carry out health needs assessments and evaluations of medical partners
- Monitor, analyse and share health and epidemiological data and assess needs and contribute to medical response planning and emergency preparedness for epidemics and mass displacement
- Cooperate with the administration team regarding budgeting and supervise the medical purchase process
- Represent MdM with authorities, partners and other NGOs on health issues
- Participate in the writing of proposals and reports

**Who you’ll work with**

You work under the supervision of the general coordinator of the mission (based in El Geneina) and in collaboration with the health advisor, the MHPSS advisor and the pharmacy officer based at HQ. You manage directly the activity manager and the pharmacy officer. In Feina, the medical team is composed of a medical team supervisor and a midwife supervisor.

**You are the right match if you:**

- Have a medical degree (medical doctor, nurse, midwife)
- Have a minimum 4 years of experience in the humanitarian sector in a similar position
- Have experience in emergency responses, outbreak management, nutrition, health assessments and medical programme start-up
- Demonstrate experience working in complex, politically sensitive or rapidly evolving environments
- Are able to work in high security context
- Have solid background in team leadership, capacity building and technical supervision
- Have strong communication, negotiation and diplomacy skills
- Have strong ability to work collaboratively with diverse teams and multicultural stakeholders
- Have excellent organisational and time-management skills
- Have mapping skills with Google Earth or ArcGIS
- Have strong proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
- Are fluent in English (spoken and written); knowledge of Arabic is an asset

**This role may not suit you if you:**

- Are not aligned with MdM’s values
- Don't have experience in volatile security environments

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.  
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

**Employment conditions**

Contract & status:

- Gross monthly salary: 3 663 €
- Fixed-term contract starting as soon as possible and for 6 months
- Single posting

Work environment:

- Position based in El Geneina , West Darfur, with regular field visits

Benefits:

- 13th month salary (paid in 2 installments after 6 months of service)

- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations

title: Mission France - Responsable des activités de travail social F/H
body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La mission France recherche un.e Responsable des activités de travail social pour son projet au Littoral Nord.

**Contexte :**

Médecins Sans Frontières intervient en France auprès des personnes exilées confrontées aux conséquences sanitaires, psychologiques et sociales des violences liées aux parcours migratoires et aux ruptures de protection. La Mission France combine soins, protection et témoignage pour répondre aux besoins des personnes les plus vulnérables.

Elle concentre aujourd’hui son action sur le Littoral Nord et l’Île-de-France, tout en conservant une capacité de réponse rapide aux situations d’urgence. Portée par des équipes pluridisciplinaires, elle développe des activités médicales, psychologiques, sociales et de plaidoyer dans un contexte en constante évolution

**Votre rôle :**

Sous la responsabilité du·de la Référent·e migration, et en lien fonctionnel avec la personne responsable de la protection de l’unité migrations, vous concevrez, superviserez et suivrez les activités de travail social du projet. Vous encadrerez les travailleur·ses sociaux·les, contribuerez à la stratégie de protection et veillerez à la qualité des accompagnements proposés.

Ce poste associe pilotage stratégique, management d’équipe et intervention directe sur le terrain : vous consacrerez notamment 30 % de votre temps aux activités de travail social, aux maraudes et à l’« aller-vers ».

**Principales responsabilités :**

Piloter Définir et piloter la stratégie de travail social et de protection

- Co-définir et mettre en œuvre la stratégie de travail social du projet, en cohérence avec les orientations opérationnelles et le cadre de travail social de MSF.
- Développer les activités autour de la gestion de cas, du soutien social aux patient·es, du lien social de première ligne et des interventions communautaires.
- Analyser le contexte et les déterminants sociaux de la santé afin d’identifier les vulnérabilités récurrentes, les situations de violence, les phénomènes de déplacement et d’exclusion, ainsi que les besoins critiques d’assistance et de protection.
- Contribuer à la définition des objectifs et des interventions de protection, notamment en matière de signalement et de prévention des risques.
- Documenter les restrictions d’accès aux services et analyser les obstacles rencontrés afin de proposer des pistes d’action et de plaidoyer en lien avec la référente médicale en migration et la mission MSF France.

**Garantir un accompagnement social de qualité et gérer les situations complexes**

- Superviser les parcours d’accompagnement social : accueil, évaluation des besoins, élaboration et mise en œuvre du plan d’intervention, orientation sécurisée, suivi et clôture des situations.
- Veiller à la prise en charge des besoins sociaux critiques, dans le périmètre du projet, par un accompagnement direct ou une orientation vers des services adaptés.
- Accompagner les équipes dans la gestion des situations complexes et intervenir directement dans les cas sensibles, notamment lorsqu’il existe des risques élevés de violence ou qu’un mineur non accompagné est concerné.
- Organiser des temps réguliers de concertation autour des situations suivies, afin de partager les difficultés et de construire des réponses adaptées avec les autres disciplines.
- Favoriser le pouvoir d’agir des personnes accompagnées en leur donnant une information claire sur leurs droits, les services disponibles, les critères d’accès et les démarches pertinentes.
- Contribuer à un environnement de soins sûr, digne et confidentiel, qui respecte les droits des patient·es et facilite l’accès aux mécanismes de retours et de plaintes.

**Développer le travail social communautaire et les partenariats**

- Participer aux maraudes et aux activités d’« aller-vers » pour identifier les besoins sociaux, les vulnérabilités et les risques de protection au sein des communautés.
- Développer, avec les équipes médicales, de santé mentale et de médiation, des interventions pluridisciplinaires visant à renforcer les facteurs de protection et de résilience.
- Construire et actualiser une cartographie des services sociaux, des associations, des partenaires institutionnels et des dispositifs communautaires présents sur la zone du projet.
- Développer des relations de coopération avec les partenaires et suivre l’accessibilité, la disponibilité et la qualité des services proposés.
- Renforcer la coordination et l’orientation des personnes vers les dispositifs adaptés, en portant une attention particulière aux situations de violence, notamment sexuelle, et aux possibilités de prise en charge.
- Contribuer à la surveillance communautaire et à l’analyse des problématiques de protection rencontrées sur le terrain.

**Manager, accompagner et développer l’équipe**

- Encadrer les travailleur·ses sociaux·les et organiser les plannings en fonction des différentes activités : maraudes, entretiens individuels et activités collectives.
- Développer les compétences de l’équipe par la formation, le coaching, la supervision et le partage de pratiques.
- Identifier les besoins de développement professionnel et mettre en œuvre un plan de développement des compétences, en lien avec le département des ressources humaines.
- Former et sensibiliser les équipes aux questions de protection, de gestion de cas, de conduite d’entretien et d’orientation.
- Contribuer aux processus de recrutement, de formation et d’évaluation des équipes concernées, en collaboration avec les RH.
- Assurer la continuité des activités en apportant un soutien opérationnel et, si nécessaire, en remplaçant les membres de l’équipe absents.
- Veiller au bien-être de l’équipe et favoriser une coopération étroite avec les autres pôles du projet.

**Assurer Suivre les activités, analyser les données et garantir la qualité**

- Superviser la collecte, l’enregistrement et l’analyse des données relatives aux activités de travail social et de protection.
- Suivre les indicateurs de résultats et produire un reporting régulier permettant d’identifier les tendances, les besoins émergents et les difficultés d’accès aux services.
- Documenter les situations et les tendances en matière de protection afin d’alimenter l’analyse opérationnelle et les actions de plaidoyer de MSF.
- Développer et adapter les outils et processus de travail social aux besoins du projet.
- Garantir le respect du cadre de travail social de MSF, des règles de confidentialité, de la protection des données et des exigences légales et éthiques.
- Planifier et coordonner les ressources humaines, matérielles et financières nécessaires aux activités, en lien avec les départements support.

**Profil recherché**

**Formation et expérience :**

- Diplôme français ou étranger de travailleur·se social·e, avec au moins trois années de formation théorique et pratique.
- Au moins trois ans d’expérience professionnelle dans la gestion de programmes de travail social ou de domaines similaires : protection, accompagnement psychosocial, violences sexuelles et basées sur le genre, etc.
- Expérience en gestion d’équipe.
- Une expérience dans un contexte sanitaire, humanitaire, de protection ou de migration est fortement souhaitée.
- Une expérience avérée en gestion de cas ou en protection dans un contexte d’urgence constitue un atout.

**Compétences et qualités :**

- Capacités d’analyse et aptitude à transformer les constats du terrain en réponses adaptées.
- Sens de l’organisation, orientation vers les résultats et exigence de qualité.
- Aptitude à manager, accompagner et développer une équipe.
- Esprit d’équipe, coopération et capacité à travailler en pluridisciplinarité.
- Sens du service et approche centrée sur la personne.
- Capacité à développer des partenariats et à construire des relations de confiance.
- Gestion du stress, flexibilité et capacité d’adaptation à des environnements changeants et difficiles.
- Permis B souhaité.

**Langues et outils :**

- Maîtrise courante du français indispensable.
- Bonne maîtrise de l’anglais à l’oral.
- La connaissance d’autres langues est fortement souhaitée.
- Maîtrise des outils informatiques courants : Word, Excel et Internet.

**Conditions d'emploi**

**Mobilité exigée sur le Littoral Nord entre Calais et Dunkerque**

Statut non-cadre : **CDD de 12 mois renouvelable**

**Rémunération et avantages :**

- **3 425,87 € brut mensuel sur 13 mois** 22 jours de RTT par an· Complémentaire santé prise en charge à 100 % par MSF·
- Titres-restaurant de 12 € (prise en charge MSF à 60 %)·
- Prise en charge à 50 % des transports en commun ou des kilomètres à vélo.

**Poste à pourvoir :** 4 janvier 2027.

*En raison de contraintes administratives liées à la durée du contrat, les candidats doivent déjà disposer d'une autorisation de travail en France (citoyen de l'Union européenne) ou d’un titre de séjour leur permettant de travailler sur le sol français.*

title: 23520 Regional Data Analyst (P)
body:
Under the overall supervision of the Deputy Regional Director (DRD) for Operations, the direct supervision of the Regional Thematic Specialist (Data and Research), and the guidance of the Chief Migration and Displacement Data and Research Analytics Division in the Department of Data, Insights and Policy, the Regional Data Analyst will focus on generating and communicating analyses and insights in support of decision-making processes. The Regional Data Analyst is responsible for leading Regional Data Hub (RDH) work on migration data analysis, focusing on migration and human mobility dynamics, including mixed migration movements, drivers, trends, and characteristics across the region.

The Regional Data Analyst will work within the RDH Team to pursue its core objective to enhance, strengthen, and promote the regional evidence base on migration and human mobility, including by addressing existing primary data gaps through innovation, insight generation, foresight and scenario building, and consolidating primary and secondary data and analysis work in the region covering migration, displacement, and human mobility.

**Responsibilities**

**Data Processing and Data Use:**

- Locate and define new data analysis process improvement opportunities.
- Identify appropriate data sources for analytics projects.
- Ensure accurate and reliable data centralization to support analytical work.
- Collaborate with Data Engineers and Data Scientists in Headquarters (HQ) or other Missions as available and needed to improve data flows, data quality, etc.
- Coordinate the development and implementation of databases, data collection systems, data analytics and other strategies that optimize statistical efficiency and quality.

**Data Analysis and Reporting:**

- Conduct and coordinate regional, sub-regional, geographic and thematic analyses and reports on issues of relevance to the current human mobility and migration dynamics in the region, paying attention to routes, trends, and patterns which may necessitate additional analysis.
- Identify gaps in migration and human mobility data, specific data needs for local, national, regional, sub-regional and global policymaking, and capacities of relevant actors on migration and human mobility data. Respond to queries on gaps identified by thematic experts. Coordinate the development of tools and mechanisms to complete data gaps, in close alignment with international approaches and standards and existing IOM-supported global mechanisms.
- Support the analysis and validation of internal, cross-border, and international migration and human mobility data collected at various points along the migration journey - at departure, en route, in destination, and upon return- stranded or in need of assistance, voluntary and forced, humanitarian evacuations, support to migrants on socioeconomic inclusion and reintegration, and strengthening their development contributions to societies.
- Use existing IOM data from global, regional, sub-regional and national projects and initiatives for data triangulation to enhance cross-thematic data analysis for regional and national reporting within the region and to strengthen evidence-based policy formulation, national and regional humanitarian and development planning and operations. Coordinate and support cross-regional analysis where relevant.
- Coordinate and support desk reviews and carry out extensive and in-depth analysis of data sources identified under the desk review.
- Identify, analyze, and interpret trends or patterns, using basic machine learning techniques, qualitative, visualization, narrative, and statistical methods to identify relevant features and variables in structured and unstructured sources of information and data.
- Coordinate the development and implementation of various analysis, reporting and quality control capabilities.
- Provide analytical support to Country Offices in the Region as needed.

**Good Data Practice, Knowledge Management and Dissemination:**

- Ensure timely preparation and generation of information products.
- Adhere to IOM data protection, governance, and security standards.
- Consider ethical data collection, use, sharing, and dissemination.
- Participate in working groups and provide strategic input on behalf of IOM.

**Cross-Cutting Issues:**

- Evaluate new applications related to information systems, to new technologies, and processes to manage information in response to RDH needs.
- Ensure the integration of disaggregated data analysis to inform gender-responsive programming, including for specific needs of people such as pregnant women, persons with disabilities, the elderly, children, as well as other highly vulnerable groups within all emergency and transition activities.
- Perform other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Migration Studies, Demography, Political or Social Science, Statistics, Econometrics, Public Health, Sustainability Science, Data Science, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with seven years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in information management, reporting, coordination, and analysis of data triangulation and analysis from multiple large and complex information systems;
- Data analysis experience (including field experience) in the area of demographic and population studies, human mobility, internal and international migration, and refugees/IDPs in developed and developing countries; remote sensing and/or Geographic Information Systems (GIS) analysis experience is also an advantage;
- Practical field experience and analysis expertise in geographic (region and/or specific countries) and thematic (displacement, migration) relevant domain;
- Experience in data collection, data processing (incl. cleaning), data analysis for research, policy, and report writing;
- Experience in internal and/or international mixed migration data analyses is required;
- Self-service analytics and data visualization applications (MS Power BI, Qlik, Tableau or similar), or business intelligence tools (SAP Business Objects, etc.) are desirable;
- Experience with database or programming languages (SQL, Python, R) is desirable; other data analysis software may be advantageous (e.g., STATA, QGIS);
- Professional experience in coordinating multi-cultural teams and field-based staff;
- Experience in survey and questionnaire design and sampling is an advantage; and,
- Knowledge of IOM data, analytical methodologies and standards is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Excellent drafting skills; Proven skills to analyse statistical information;
- Ability to formulate IM-related technical requirements and operating procedures;
- Ability to translate planning specifications into technical briefs for data capture and analysis, and vice versa;
- Ability to compile and holistically analyse diverse datasets;
- Demonstrated team-building and information management skills; and,
- Demonstrated understanding of different data analysis methodologies.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

title: 23673 Programme Coordinator (Immigration and Border Governance (IBG)) (P)
Procurement Manager, Emerging Technology and Digital Innovation Procurement
body:
**Background**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to humanitarian crises in over 40 countries and in communities across the United States and Europe, helping people whose lives have been shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and rebuild their futures.

Global Procurement, within the Global Supply Chain function, leads sourcing strategy, category management, and supplier management for the organization. As IRC continues to test and adopt new technology to support its mission, Global Procurement is establishing a dedicated Procurement Manager role to provide procurement capacity for emerging technology and digital innovation.

**Position Overview**

The Procurement Manager, Emerging Technology and Digital Innovation Procurement supports fast-moving technology sourcing needs across IRC, with a focus on early-stage digital innovation, pilots, proofs of concept, trials, and emerging tools. The role helps teams test and evaluate new technology quickly while maintaining procurement discipline, vendor due diligence, risk review, documentation, and compliance.

For this role, “digital innovation” refers to early-stage, small-scale, fast-moving technology initiatives where IRC teams are testing a new idea, tool, platform, vendor, or digital approach before deciding whether to scale. The portfolio covers AI and generative AI tools where applicable, SaaS and digital platforms, automation, data and analytics, migration and testing tools, cybersecurity tools, collaboration platforms, digital service delivery tools, field and mobile technology, low-code and no-code platforms, and other emerging digital solutions.

This role is an execution-focused, hands-on individual contributor role. It enables IRC to move quickly on emerging technology and digital innovation requests without bypassing procurement controls, vendor due diligence, information security, data protection, legal review, donor compliance, or documentation requirements. The Procurement Manager serves as the day-to-day procurement focal point for these requests

**Key Responsibilities**

**A. Emerging Technology and Digital Innovation Sourcing Execution**

- Provide hands-on sourcing support for pilots, trials, proofs of concept, small-scale SaaS, emerging vendors, startup-style tools, and digital innovation requests across IRC.
- Execute sourcing activities in line with the IT category strategy and under the guidance of the Senior Category Manager, IT.
- Conduct early market scans and market intelligence for emerging tools, vendors, pricing models, and digital innovation categories.
- Support requirements gathering, supplier identification, RFI/RFQ/RFP preparation, evaluation support, award recommendation, and contract finalization.
- Build supplier visibility for innovation and emerging technology vendors, including startup and niche providers that may later become larger enterprise solutions.
- Help bring new tools into proper procurement channels, reducing shadow IT, credit-card purchasing, and unmanaged technology spend.
- Support SaaS rationalization, renewal planning, demand management, and license optimization at the innovation and pilot tier.
- Help business teams translate technical needs into clear scopes of work, evaluation criteria, and vendor questions.

**B. Pilot, Trial, and Proof-of-Concept Procurement Frameworks**

- Build and maintain a lightweight, repeatable procurement pathway for pilots, trials, and proofs of concept.
- Develop checklists, decision tools, and methodology for short-term technology engagements.
- Define the minimum documentation required before a pilot, trial, or proof of concept can begin.
- Maintain clear approval checkpoints and escalation criteria so teams understand when a pilot can proceed and when it requires further review.
- Track emerging technology requests from intake through pilot, decision, and possible scale-up.
- Ensure required reviews and approvals are completed and all necessary checks are documented before tools are tested or used.
- Help document whether a pilot should end, continue, scale, or move into a formal sourcing process.
- Coordinate NDAs and pre-procurement documentation when teams need to test or evaluate multiple tools before selecting a vendor.
- Ensure pilots and trials are set up in a way that allows long-term success if IRC later moves to a larger phase or formal sourcing process.

**C. AI-Enabled and High-Risk Technology Procurement Support**

- Support sourcing for AI-enabled tools as part of the broader emerging technology portfolio, applied only when AI functionality is in scope.
- For AI-enabled tools, support the application of IRC’s AI assessment requirements, including use-case risk classification, provider/deployer determination, GenAI tool checks, and required approvals.
- Coordinate with the AI Governance and Risk Committee and AI Department Focal Points when applicable.
- Identify and escalate sourcing requests that may involve high-risk technology, AI functionality, personal information, confidential data, client-facing tools, cybersecurity concerns, or unapproved tools.
- Support procurement documentation for AI-enabled tools, including evidence of approvals, vendor assessments, risk reviews, and contract requirements.

**D. Vendor Due Diligence, Risk Review, and Documentation**

- Coordinate required vendor risk assessments (VRA) and due diligence across cybersecurity, privacy and data protection, legal, donor compliance, sanctions and ATC screening, financial viability, implementation risk, integration risk, operational support model, and vendor lock-in and exit risk.
- Coordinate with Information Security, Data Protection, Office of General Counsel, Risk and Compliance, and Finance to ensure required reviews are completed before pilots, trials, awards, or contract signature.
- Ensure procurement files are complete, audit-ready, and aligned with IRC sourcing policy and donor requirements.
- Support compliance with institutional donor requirements that may affect technology, AI, data hosting, data residency, and vendor selection.
- Track and follow up on missing documentation, approvals, vendor information, and risk reviews.

**E. Tool and Vendor Visibility**

- Maintain or support a list of emerging technology tools and vendors, indicating status (under review, in pilot, approved, rejected, expired) and the approved use case for each tool.
- Document the business owner, contract status, contract dates, and renewal timing for each tool.
- Document what each tool is approved for and what use would require additional approval or new procurement action.
- Help connect business owners, end users, IT, Procurement, Information Security, Data Protection, Legal, and Finance around emerging technology tools and vendors.
- Reduce situations where approved tools are used in non-approved ways, and flag misuse for review.

**F. Contracting and Commercial Support**

- Support commercial negotiation and contracting across the emerging technology portfolio, including NDAs, trial agreements, pilot agreements, proof-of-concept agreements, SaaS agreements, subscriptions, software licenses, cloud services, implementation services, and renewals.
- Review pricing models, including seat-based licensing, usage-based pricing, token usage, API calls, implementation fees, renewal escalators, and support fees, and provide commercial analysis.
- Coordinate with Legal, IT, Finance, and business owners to ensure contracts include appropriate terms on data protection, confidentiality, intellectual property, service levels, audit rights, incident reporting, termination, data return, and exit provisions.
- For AI-enabled tools, ensure contracts also address AI-generated outputs, model training restrictions, and AI-specific risk allocation.
- Support renewal planning and help prevent last-minute renewals or unplanned vendor commitments.

**G. Stakeholder Engagement and Service Support**

- Provide practical, service-oriented procurement support to teams exploring new tools, pilots, digital services, automation platforms, AI solutions, or other emerging technology.
- Help stakeholders move through the procurement process without unnecessary delays, while maintaining compliance and risk controls.
- Coordinate between business owners, IT owners, Procurement, end users, Information Security, Data Protection, Legal, and Finance to ensure tool usage remains aligned with approved scope, contract terms, procurement files, risk approvals, and any applicable usage guidelines.
- Reduce workarounds, shadow IT, and credit-card purchasing by making the correct procurement process easier to follow.
- Guide stakeholders on procurement routes, required documentation, approval steps, and realistic timelines for emerging technology procurement.
- Support early engagement with teams considering new tools, pilots, or digital approaches, before commitments are made to vendors.

**H. Reporting and Continuous Improvement**

- Track the emerging technology sourcing pipeline, renewal calendar, cycle time, savings, risk flags, documentation completion, and approval status.
- Track pilot outcomes (end, continue, scale, or formal sourcing) and capture lessons learned.
- Track user adoption issues, non-approved usage of approved tools, and other compliance signals, and surface these to the Senior Category Manager, IT.
- Identify recurring issues in emerging technology sourcing and recommend improvements to frameworks, checklists, templates, and decision tools.
- Contribute to knowledge sharing across Global Procurement on emerging technology, SaaS, AI, and digital innovation sourcing practices.
- Support the role’s value contribution by improving visibility over fast-moving technology spend, reducing duplicated tools, undocumented pilots, and audit risk.

**Key Working Relationships**

- **Reports to:** Senior Category Manager, IT.
- **Internal:** Office of the CIO and IT teams; Senior Category Manager, IT; Information Security; Data Protection; Office of General Counsel; Ethics and Compliance; Risk and Compliance; Finance; Airbel Impact Lab; Data and Analytics; External Relations; Country Program supply chain and innovation leads; program innovation teams; fundraising and digital teams; AI Governance and Risk Committee when applicable; Global Procurement peers.
- **External:** Emerging technology vendors and resellers; SaaS, cloud, cybersecurity, automation, data, and AI providers; startup and niche technology vendors; industry analysts; peer humanitarian and development organizations.

**Minimum Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree in procurement, supply chain, business administration, information technology, engineering, law, or a related field. Equivalent experience may be considered.
- Minimum 5 to 7 years of procurement, sourcing, contract management, or vendor management experience.
- Of the required 5 to 7 years above, at least 3 years must be in IT procurement, SaaS and software sourcing, software licensing, cloud services, cybersecurity tools, data platforms, or similar technology categories.
- Experience supporting pilots, trials, proofs of concept, or other early-stage technology procurement activities.

body:

**Context:**

Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) in Fiji and the direct supervision of the Project Manager (PM), the National Project Officer – Disability Inclusion will be responsible and accountable for supporting the implementation of programming related to disaster displacements and strengthening resilience to disasters and climate change-related fragility in Solomon Islands. The position will also support programming aimed at strengthening the resilience of persons with disabilities, youth, older persons and women. In addition, the incumbent will support the design and implementation of disability-inclusive early warning systems (EWS), the development of related information, education and communication (IEC) materials, delivery of relevant inclusive trainings, and Community-Based Disaster Response Management (CBDRM).  
The incumbent will support community level activities, coordinate with government partners (both national and provincial), and directly work with persons with disabilities, youth, women and older persons.

**Description for Internal Candidates**

**Responsibilities for Internal Candidates**

1. Under the supervision of the Project Manager, assist in the implementation and monitoring of activities related to disaster preparedness and response, including the coordination of the financial, logistical, administrative and technical aspects in accordance with IOM’s policies.

3. Monitor project implementation against approved work plans; document and evaluate results; identify gaps, deviations and bottlenecks; keep the supervisor informed; and suggest actions to improve implementation.
4. Contribute to the integration and mainstreaming of gender, protection, human rights and other pertinent cross-cutting issues into programme implementation.
5. Assist in identifying potential areas for project development and contribute to the development of new projects by selecting and summarizing background information, assessing the local context and drafting segments of project proposals.

**Experience**

- Experience implementing programming related to climate change and human mobility and/or disaster risk reduction, including CBDRM, disaster risk reduction (DRR) Preparedness, and EWS;
- Experience in liaising with governmental authorities, national/international institutions, United Nations agencies and non-governmental organizations;
- Experience supporting the design and implementation of accessible and inclusive programming for persons with disabilities, youth, older persons and women, preferably in a disaster-preparedness or disaster-risk-reduction context;

title: Strategy and Planning Senior Officer, Global Policy & Advocacy
body:
**Background**: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) helps people affected by humanitarian crises to survive, recover and rebuild their lives. We deliver lasting impact by providing health care, helping children learn, and empowering individuals and communities to become self-reliant, always with a focus on the unique needs of women and girls. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, we now work in over 40 crisis-affected countries as well as communities throughout the U.S., Europe and Latin America.

The External Relations (ER) Department mobilizes external audiences to raise the requisite funds, influence policies and achieve practice changes to improve outcomes for our clients, while growing and protecting our global brand. The Global Policy & Advocacy team is a dynamic part of the ER Department that leverages the power of IRC’s ideas to solve the biggest challenges facing IRC’s clients across the “arc of crisis” and influence external stakeholders, in particular governments and multi-lateral institutions, to enact these solutions to ultimately make meaningful change for our clients. From addressing the drivers of conflict to meeting the needs of displaced people, the team partners with innovative thinkers, experts and those with lived experience to identify solutions and bring them to life. We take pride in being solutions-oriented and creative. We are precise in our goals, tactics, and messages. We drive change year over year, knowing that system change takes dedicated focus while maintaining the flexibility to respond to emerging needs across the globe. Finally, we are collaborative, constantly seeking new ideas and perspectives from others in our sector and beyond as we work side by side with programs, strategy, communications and research and innovation teams across the IRC.

**Job Overview/Summary:**

The Strategy and Planning Senior Officer will lead on key strategic planning and prioritization efforts for the Policy & Advocacy team. The Senior Officer will coordinate portions of organization-wide strategy and investment planning, collaborate with the Vice President of Policy & Advocacy on team prioritization processes, and manage a collaborative but streamlined process for strategy development. This person will maintain crucial processes and relationships and collaborate at all levels within and across the teams, and across the IRC.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- **Facilitate priority-setting processes:** Translate organization-wide strategy and policy products into department strategies, market-specific advocacy priorities, and thematic policy areas of focus.
- **Lead strategy development processes:** Work closely with Policy and Advocacy team members to support the development of specific, actionable policy and advocacy strategies, helping individual units develop strategies relevant to their priority issues and their geographic/political markets that include stakeholder mapping, activity planning, product development plans, and desired external change metrics as relevant. Lead Policy and Advocacy engagement in organization-wide annual planning processes, linking Policy and Advocacy planning to multi-year organizational strategies and Department-wide objectives.
- **Develop and facilitate activities and processes across Policy and Advocacy teams:** Facilitate and maintain efficient ways of working within, across, and with the Policy and Advocacy teams as appropriate. Identify and elevate collaboration challenges and develop ways of working systems to address those issues. Ensure ways of working are routinely updated to address feedback from team members and represent team in org-wide, multi-departmental process conversations.
- **Manage long-term projects**: Own project management, strategic content development, and logistics for key team efforts such as the Annual Planning and Quarterly Pause processes, retreat planning, and others.
- **Facilitate cross-team collaboration and communication:** Create tools and processes for effectively sharing information and collaborating internally, communicating with IRC stakeholders routinely, and managing workflows in a streamlined and smooth manner. Facilitate regular, effective, and efficient communication between team members and from organizational leadership to the rest of the teams, cascading information from ER leadership, finance, and HR as necessary. Manage the internal website and routine reporting to senior leaders. Develop deep understanding of Policy and Advocacy priorities and strategies in order to communicate effectively about team objectives and outcomes with internal stakeholders through reporting processes, internal websites, email and other means as appropriate.
- **Lead KPI development and progress tracking:** Working with the VP and members of the Policy and Advocacy team develop a set of high-level objectives for teams alongside a more detailed set of KPIs to enable reporting out to the organization on progress. Plan and facilitate quarterly internal progress reviews of individual strategies (and associated metrics) across Policy and Advocacy. Ensure KPIs and reporting metrics are logical, consistent, and regularly reported on by team members on a weekly basis.
- **Teamwork:** Support a positive team culture by acting openly and collaboratively, supporting colleagues in their work and sharing credit with others where appropriate. Organize team retreats, staff meetings, team building activities and trainings.

title: Project Director, Virtual Services
body:
**Job Overview:**

The Project Director of Virtual Services at the International Rescue Committee (IRC) provides strategic leadership and operational oversight of a national portfolio of virtual resettlement programs that expand access to essential services for refugees and other newcomers across the United States, particularly those living outside traditional service areas. The portfolio includes legacy resettlement programs, state-run programs as well as [ALMA](https://welcome.rescue.org/us/en/services/alma), an AI-powered virtual assistant that helps newcomers navigate essential resources and services. The Project Director also contributes to the Resettlement, Asylum and Integration Department’s virtual and information services strategy.

The role oversees virtual program strategy, implementation, performance, and budget management. It also ensures compliance with award requirements through programmatic monitoring and rigorous direct assistance operations, and it oversees the case management and data systems that support reporting and evidence of impact. The Director leads a geographically dispersed team and cultivates partnerships with government agencies, nonprofit organizations, and other stakeholders. A central focus of the position is developing and scaling innovative, technology-enabled service delivery models that strengthen operational efficiency and promote client self-sufficiency. This position reports to the Senior Director of Resettlement.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- **Program Implementation**: Lead the design, implementation, and scaling of a national portfolio of virtual programs (some examples include Program of Initial Resettlement, Matching Grant, Preferred Communities) that expand access to essential services for refugees and other newcomers across the United States, leveraging innovative, client-centered service delivery models to reach underserved populations.
- **Interagency Collaboration:** Provide strategic leadership and oversight of interagency virtual services working groups, fostering collaboration and alignment across resettlement agencies to inform program strategy, coordinate implementation, and strengthen virtual service delivery.
- **People & Culture:** Build and cultivate an inclusive, impactful team. Support managers in their leadership of teams in line with IRC's People Manager Standards to ensure successful program delivery and a safe, supportive environment for clients and staff.
- **Monitoring & Compliance:** Design and enable effective monitoring, evaluation, and reporting on program services. Ensure a data-driven approach that informs program adaptation and provides further evidence of virtual services impact.
- **Budget & Financial Management:** Coordinate with HQ Finance staff to ensure compliance with donor and organizational requirements including financial planning, expenditure monitoring, caseload forecasting, and effective resource allocation.
- **AI Product Strategy and Management:** Lead the product strategy, development, and deployment of ALMA, IRC's AI-powered virtual assistant, in collaboration with the Airbel Impact Lab and IRC's technical development teams. Oversee product roadmaps, iterative development, testing, and the rollout of new features and international adaptations, including expansion to Poland.
- **Client Engagement and Co-Design:** Lead IRC's Service Excellence Advisory Committee, creating structured opportunities for refugees and other newcomers to inform program design, implementation, and continuous improvement. Integrate client feedback and lived experiences into service delivery, technology development, and strategic decision-making.
- **Technical Expertise and Resource Mobilization:** Provide technical expertise and strategic input into the development of grant proposals, funding opportunities, and program designs that expand and strengthen virtual service delivery across IRC's resettlement network. Identify and apply for opportunities to advance virtual services.
- **Strategic Partnerships and Stakeholder Engagement:** Cultivate and maintain partnerships with government agencies, national resettlement organizations, and other key stakeholders to advance virtual service delivery, strengthen interagency coordination, and identify opportunities for program expansion.
- Other related duties as assigned.

- Minimum 5-7 years of progressively responsible work experience with refugee resettlement; experience and deep familiarity with initial resettlement programming.

**Entrée en fonction :** 1.12.26

**Durée :** 6 mois

**Lieu :** Dakar, Sénégal

**Statut :** non accompagné

Terre des hommes ne fixe pas de date de clôture pour ce poste ; le recrutement se poursuit jusqu'à ce que le poste soit pourvu.

**Tdh :**

La Fondation Terre des hommes (Tdh), dont le siège est à Lausanne et le bureau à Zurich, est la plus grande organisation suisse de défense des droits de l'enfant avec plus de 2000 collaborateurs et collaboratrices dans le monde. Nous nous engageons aux côtés des enfants pour garantir leurs droits, protéger leur vie et améliorer leur bien-être. Nous y parvenons grâce à nos programmes innovants dans les domaines de la santé, de la migration et de l'accès à la justice, conçus pour avoir un impact positif et durable.

**Contexte :**

Terre des hommes Lausanne (Tdh), fondée en 1960, est la plus grande organisation suisse de défense des droits de l'enfant. Tdh se consacre à apporter des changements significatifs et durables dans la vie des enfants et des jeunes, en particulier ceux et celles qui sont le plus en danger. Tdh est active dans une trentaine de pays, dans des contextes humanitaires et de développement.

En Afrique subsaharienne, Tdh intervient directement dans 8 pays (Burkina Faso, Burundi, Guinée-Conakry, Kenya Mali, Mauritanie, Nigeria et Sénégal,) et via des partenariats dans 6 autres pays (Benin, Cameroun, Madagascar, Niger, Togo et Ouganda).

Dans le cadre de la décentralisation de son modèle d'organisation, Tdh à ouvert un bureau régional à Dakar au Sénégal pour lequel un poste de Chargé.e des Opérations est ouvert.

**Responsabilités :**

Sous la supervision de la Conseillère Régionale en recherche de fonds, le.la Chargé.e des Opérations appuie le bureau régional et les équipes pays dans la mise en œuvre des activités liées aux subventions et à la collecte de fonds dans la région Afrique.

Ce poste contribue aux processus relatifs aux subventions et à la collecte de fonds — du suivi des opportunités à l'élaboration des propositions et au reporting auprès des bailleurs — tout en soutenant les efforts en matière d'engagement des bailleurs et de partenariats à l'échelle de la région.

Grant Acquisition Process

- Contribue à l'identification et au suivi des opportunités de financement pertinentes pour les programmes de Tdh dans la région Afrique.
- Appuie le développement et la soumission de propositions de projet régionales, multipays et pays : appui ou coordination du processus d’écriture, respect des procédures bailleurs, développement de plans d’action, écriture, traduction, enregistrement sur les plateformes de soumission.
- Contribue au contrôle qualité et à la finalisation des rapports pour des financements institutionnels tout en s’assurant de la soumission en temps voulu (suivi du calendrier et des échéances, relances lorsque nécessaire auprès des contributeurs, consolidation des données, etc.), conformément aux exigences contractuelles et aux normes de Tdh.
- Assure le suivi des besoins en cofinancement avec la CR Finance, appui l'élaboration de propositions et rapports de projets à destination de fondations en coordination avec le secteur philanthropie.
- Veille à ce que les informations relatives aux subventions et aux financements dans Engage360 et les GFU pays et région (système interne de Tdh) soient exactes et régulièrement mises à jour, et assure le suivi auprès des équipes concernées pour garantir l'exhaustivité des données. En cas d’absence de Chargé.e de Grant dans une délégation, assure directement la mise à jour des données pour le pays concerné.
- Appuie le développement des contrats de partenariats opérationnels (contenu, signature, archivage, etc.).
- Contribue à l’analyse des réponses aux demandes de financements institutionnels et philanthropiques.
- S’assure de la collecte et de l’archivage des documents institutionnels nécessaires à la signature des contrats en collaboration avec le siège, la région, les délégations et les partenaires.

Communication

- Appuie la relation avec les bailleurs de fonds et les partenaires, y compris la préparation de supports de recherche de fonds (ex. : témoignages, récits de réussite).
- Appuie le rapportage annuel à travers la vérification et la consolidation des données et informations projets, en coordination avec les équipes PREX, Q&A et Grants, ainsi qu’avec les autres parties prenantes concernées aux niveaux des délégations et de la région.
- Contribue à la communication interne liée aux projets (newsletter mensuelle, supports spécifiques, etc.) et consolide les éléments proposés par les délégations et la région, en veillant à la cohérence, à l’exactitude et à la qualité des informations rapportées.

*La description complète du poste sera communiquée aux candidats sélectionnés pour lancer le processus de recrutement.*

**Profil recherché**

**Formation :**

Etude supérieure (Master ou autre diplôme équivalant en relations internationales, développement ou autre domaine pertinent)

**Langues :**

Excellentes compétences linguistiques en Français et Anglais.

**Compétences :**

- Bonne compréhension de la gestion du cycle de projet dans les environnements de développement, d'urgence et de crises prolongées, notamment en Afrique
- Bonne compréhension du processus d’aquisition de financements.

**IT :** Maitrise des outils et applications usuels (Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, etc.)

**Conditions :**

Contrat suisse

Salaire mensuel brut CHF 2450- x13,36 mois

Assurances : maladie, accident, rapatriement

Congés annuels : 25 jours/an

Vols aller-retour vers le lieu d'affectation

**Code Global de Conduite et Politiques Ethiques de Tdh :**

S'engage à promouvoir et à respecter le Code de Conduite Global, à rapporter systématiquement toute violation du Code à travers les mécanismes formels de rapport de Tdh et à traiter toute violation des procédures et des processus de manière appropriée.

Sensibilise la Fondation aux risques de non-respect des politiques, de violence et d'abus, et aux droits qui en découlent, à l'égard des enfants, des membres de la communauté et de nos propres employé.e.s.

S'engage à respecter les principales politiques et directives éthiques, notamment la politique de sauvegarde, la politique de lutte contre la fraude et la corruption, la politique relative aux conflits d'intérêts et d'autres politiques liées à la prévention du financement du terrorisme et des activités criminelles, ainsi qu’au comportement sur le lieu de travail.

S'engage à mettre en pratique les valeurs et les principes en adoptant un comportement exemplaire, en parfaite adéquation avec le code de conduite, et en respectant toujours les procédures et les processus établis.

S'engage à développer une culture de management conforme et éclairée au sein de l'organisation et dans notre travail avec les enfants et les communautés dans lesquelles nous opérons.

title: Protection Coordinator
body:
**About the job**

**Overall purpose of the role:** Based in the DRC Türkiye country office, the role provides technical oversight to DRC Protection programme, including to strategy and proposal development, reporting, technical guidance and guidelines, technical support for DRC and partner staff, as well as advising on protection research, needs assessment(s), and advocacy efforts.

**Geographic Scope: Country (Türkiye)**

The role is based in the DRC Türkiye Country Office in Gaziantep.

**Duties and Responsibilities:**

***Protection Sectoral Technical Responsibility***

- Technically responsible for the overall protection portfolio, with a strong focus on protection analysis, partnerships, and multi-partner coordination
- With the support of the Partnerships Coordinator, Head of Programme, and Senior Management Team, continue shaping and operationalising DRC’s localisation approach to protection programming and identifying innovative ways to collaborate with CSOs, national and grassroots organisations including refugee-led organisations beyond formal partnership agreements. This will include capacity development and technical support to existing and new partners
- Lead multi-partner protection monitoring analysis efforts in line with the Protection Analysis Framework (PAF) tailored to the Türkiye context
- Lead the development and implementation of the country level protection strategy
- Oversee and lead the in-country development, harmonisation, adaptation and rollout of internal policies, guidelines, tools, Standard Operating Procedures, related to DRC’s protection interventions
- Act as a reference point for Economic Recovery colleagues for Protection Mainstreaming & integrated programming
    
     ***Technical Supervision***
- Technically supervise, provide technical advice and guidance to protection staff at Country Office level, including a Protection Programme Officer and a Protection Analysis Officer
- Participate in human resource processes, including the recruitment of protection technical staff in country, establishing minimum technical requirements for protection positions, and supporting performance objectives and performance appraisals
- Responsible for identifying protection sectoral technical gaps and establishing & delivering capacity building plans for protection staff
    
    ***Protection Programme Development and Oversight***
- Lead and contribute to the design and finalisation of all protection sectoral interventions in proposals and projects
- Provide technical review of all proposals that include protection interventions and/or mainstreaming
- Maintain oversight of overall protection programme implementation, including budgets and indicators, in close collaboration with HoP, MEAL, Grants & Partnerships, and Finance colleagues
- Participate in protection programme / project review meetings, including grant opening, grant review and close out meetings
    
     ***Quality Assurance***
- Lead, in collaboration with MEAL team, on the development of quality assurance systems and ensure they are applied throughout the programme cycle
- Follow technical oversight mechanisms to ensure protection interventions are provided according to established policies, guidance, and Standard Operating Procedures
- Lead the self-assessment based on the Protection Programme Quality Framework once a year and contribute to the annual Protection Survey
    
     ***Coordination and Representation***
- Represent DRC and actively contribute to protection sector coordination fora at the country level
- Lead DRC’s protection sector coordination and collaboration efforts with relevant stakeholders including government, civil society, NGOs, and UN
- Actively engage and contribute to DRC protection-related advocacy efforts, nationally as well as regionally
- Promote integrated programming and ensure internal coordination and harmonisation of DRC protection interventions across sites and with other core sectors, as relevant
    
    ***Other***
- Any other duties as requested by the line manager

**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect you to have university degree in law, social science, political science, international development, or any other related field.

Moreover, we also expect the following:

*Required*

- Minimum 5 years of demonstrated technical experience in the international protection sector preferably with an (I)NGO and/or UN agencies
- Minimum 3 years of experience leading, managing or providing technical advice/support to a protection programme that preferably includes legal counselling and assistance, case management and protection monitoring programming
- Very strong technical writing skills
- Documented skills in project development and design for protection programmes, preferably in a multisectoral setting
- Experience in protection strategy development including the development of SOPs, training materials and action plans
- Strategic thinker with the ability to quickly develop good insight and understanding of humanitarian, political and human rights situation in the relevant context
- Proven strong analytical thinker and problem solver
- Experience with technical supervision of teams
- Experience in providing technical guidance and developing and providing learning activities
- Experience working with key institutional donors such as ECHO, DANIDA and SIDA on protection
- Experience in driving protection partnerships including with refugee-led organisations, national partners, local/government authorities, UN organizations and coordination networks
- Full professional proficiency in written and spoken English
- Turkish and/or Arabic proficiency an added value

*Desired*

- Experience in advocacy for protection a strong asset
- Experience working on mixed migration programming a strong asset

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:

**Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**We offer**

Contract length: Initially until 31.12.2027 (with possible extension based on fund availability and performance)

Band: G1 – Non-Manager

Designation of Duty Station: Country Office (Gaziantep)

Start date: 01.12.2026

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for nationals or expatriates and depends on the successful candidate’s profile. For questions regarding the vacancy please reach out to us by sending email to TUR-Recruitment@drc.ngo

title: HEAD Of Middle East Durable Solutions Platform
body:
The Danish Refugee Council assists refugees and internally displaced persons across the globe: we provide emergency aid, fight for their rights, and strengthen their opportunity for a brighter future. We work in conflict-affected areas, along the displacement routes, and in the countries where refugees settle. In cooperation with local communities, we strive for responsible and sustainable solutions. We work toward successful integration and – whenever possible – for the fulfilment of the wish to return home.

The Danish Refugee Council was founded in Denmark in 1956, and has since grown to become an international humanitarian organization with more than 7,000 staff and 8,000 volunteers. Our vision is a dignified life for all displaced.

All of our efforts are based on our value compass: humanity, respect, independence and neutrality, participation.

DRC hosts the Middle East Durable Solutions Platform (ME DSP), a membership-based NGO platform established by DRC, NRC and IRC and later joined by Oxfam, ACF and Save the Children to strengthen evidence, programming and advocacy on solutions to displacement in and from Syria. In 2022 its scope was widened to Iraq and Yemen. Following a period of hibernation since 2023, ME DSP has secured core donor funding and is in the process of re-establishing its membership, reviewing its governance and operating model, and diversify its partnerships. ME DSP is one of three DRC-hosted solutions platforms, alongside ReDSS (East Africa and Great Lakes) and ADSP (Asia), and sits within the DRC Middle East, Asia and Europe Hub under the leadership of the Hub’s Executive Director.

The **Head of ME DSP** provides overall leadership, strategic direction and management of the Platform, a membership-based, consensus-driven platform of NGOs working on solutions to displacement across the Middle East. As the Platform’s principal convener, s/he leads engagement with members and governance structures, builds consensus around shared priorities and ensures delivery of agreed commitments; leads the Platform’s evidence, learning and policy agenda so that research is translated into programming and policy guidance; represents the Platform at senior level with members, governments and donors, UN agencies and policy makers at country regional and global levels; manages ME DSP grants, staff and consultants; and works in close collaboration with DRC’s sister platforms, ReDSS and ADSP.

**Responsibilities:**

**Strategic Leadership, Governance and Management**

- Facilitate the implementation of the ME DSP Strategy 2026-2028, lead the regular review of the Platform’s work plans, and ensure ME DSP maintains a strategic, neutral and member-driven role that complements existing coordination mechanisms
- Lead the re-establishment of the Platform’s membership and the review of its governance and operating model, in line with Steering Committee decisions
- Lead annual planning and budgeting and report to the Steering Committee and members on progress, risks and results; maintain the risk matrix, commission periodic evaluation of ME DSP and integrate lessons learned
- Work in close collaboration with ReDSS and ADSP to share learning, align approaches and tools, and contribute to joint NGO engagement in global solutions fora
- Accountable for people management of direct reports, including recruitment, objective setting, performance management and staff development, and for the management of ME DSP consultants

**Membership Convening and Coordination**

- Act as the Platform’s principal convener. Design and facilitate member meetings, technical working groups and consultations in an inclusive and transparent manner that builds collective ownership of the Platform’s agenda and outputs
- Facilitate consensus-building among members, managing differing priorities and resolving issues that may affect Platform decisions and delivery
- Ensure effective coordination and information sharing among members and the Steering Committee, and support members’ engagement with the Platform at country, regional and global levels
- Lead a membership engagement strategy, including the onboarding of new members and clarity on members’ roles and contributions.

**Research, Evidence and Learning**

- Define and oversee the Platform’s research and knowledge management agenda with members, initiating and commissioning studies, managing researchers and research institutions, and ensuring methodologically rigorous, research ethics and relevance to programming and policy
- Lead the analysis of regional displacement and solutions data, strategies, policies and legislation; translate evidence into programming and policy guidance, briefing papers and policy briefs; and ensure quality control of all ME DSP publications and monitoring of their uptake
- Facilitate regular technical workshops and learning events and the roll-out of learning tools and training packages, ensuring cross-learning across countries and with global developments in solutions policy and practice
- Promote the meaningful engagement of displacement-affected communities and local civil society in the Platform’s evidence, learning and policy work

**Policy Engagement and External Representation**

- Represent the Platform at senior level with governments and national authorities, donors, UN agencies, international financial institutions, regional bodies and policy makers, building trusted relationships and navigating politically sensitive contexts with discretion and in line with humanitarian principles
- Oversee the development and implementation of the Platform’s policy and advocacy strategy with members, ensuring positions are evidence-based, agreed by members and coordinated with NGO fora and durable solutions working groups in the region
- Support members’ advocacy with governmental and inter-governmental actors and engage proactively in regional and global policy processes on solutions for displacement-affected populations
- Engage research institutions, think tanks and academia, and oversee high-quality external communications reflecting members’ agreed positions

**Business Development and Project Management**

- Manage existing and future grants, including budgets, work plans, monitoring and donor reporting, ensuring timely delivery and compliance with DRC and donor policies, including safeguarding
- Develop and implement a fundraising strategy to ensure financial sustainability, including donor engagement and partnerships, in coordination with the Steering Committee

**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect you to have **Experience and technical competencies** :

- Advanced university degree or equivalent in political science, international relations, humanitarian law, migration, Middle East studies, or related field
- Understanding of the regional displacement dynamics. Excellent understanding of
- At least 8 years' relevant experience, including 5 in people management and substantial experience leading, facilitating or coordinating a membership-based, consensus-driven consortium, network, NGO forum or inter-agency platform
- Expert knowledge of durable solutions to displacement and the relevant international frameworks, with demonstrated experience in complex and contested return and reintegration contexts
- In-depth knowledge of the displacement context of the Middle East, displacement in and from Syria, Iraq and Yemen, and of the political complexities, policy landscape and coordination architecture of the region
- Demonstrated strategic leadership, ability to manage competing priorities, and ensure accountability for results
- Proven experience in grant management, budget oversight and resource mobilization
- Proven experience in leading, conducting or commissioning research, or in working in close collaboration with researchers, and in translating evidence into programming and policy guidance
- Excellent convening, facilitation and networking skills, with the ability to build trust and broker consensus among diverse organizations; outstanding interpersonal and diplomatic skills, political and cultural sensitivity, tact and impartiality
- Excellent analytical and writing skills, with proven experience producing high quality research and policy briefs and presenting complex information in an accessible manner
- Demonstrated commitment to collaborative working across organizations and with sister platforms, ability to work in a multicultural environment, and flexibility, proactive engagement and high tolerance for change, complexity and unpredictability

**In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:**

**Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You act in line with DRC’s vision and values.

**Application process**

All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV (no longer than four pages) in English. **Applications sent by email will not be considered.**

*Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and we encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible. We reserve the right to close the vacancy before the advertised deadline if a suitable candidate is identified.* “

If you have questions or are facing problems with the online application process, please visit [drc.ngo/jobsupport](https://forms-hr.drc.dk/view.php?id=348161).
